compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'add that alongside our existing portability invariant as an agent guidance rule for this project: keeping rebar portable means it working across environments with diverse CI providers or no CI provider.'

Discovered via the compaction redesign: story A dropped the operation-linked compaction trigger and story B replaced it with a GitHub-Actions-only schedule — silently breaking any adopter with no CI. rebar already has a portability invariant with teeth: the blocking plan-review criterion `project.portability`, activated by `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and detected by `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`. Its `Platform and venue` matrix cell reads "macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD, CI, servers, developer workstations" — one undifferentiated `CI` cell. Under it, a plan triggered only by GitHub Actions names a supported cell and draws no finding, because neither "a different CI provider" nor "no CI provider at all" is a nameable alternate shape. That is the gap.

## Approach
One authoritative wording, in the criterion's detection text; everything else points at it.

1. **Extend the criterion's detection text** — `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`:
   - split the `Platform and venue` matrix cell so both alternate shapes are nameable: "macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD, CI under any provider (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and others), projects with NO CI provider at all, servers, developer workstations."
   - add one rule under the matrix, in the rubric's cause-and-effect style: a capability whose ONLY trigger is a specific CI system is not portable; a plan scheduling recurring or automatic work must state an operation-linked or in-process fallback, and one that does not is a finding whose alternate shape is "a project with no CI provider" and whose observable breakage is "the capability never runs at all."
   The four-element finding threshold and the Non-findings guard are untouched, so silence about CI stays a non-finding and configured, opt-in CI behavior stays allowed — only a hard dependency fires.
2. **Pin the new detection text** — `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py::test_client_shape_matrix` asserts the `Platform and venue` value as an exact string, so it carries the new value; add a sibling assertion for the no-CI-provider rule so it cannot be silently dropped.
3. **Update the one hand-authored mirror** — `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Dogfooding a project portability guard" reproduces the matrix verbatim (line 397), and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py::test_client_shape_matrix` (line 94) pins that copy as an exact string. The doc mirror must carry the same new cell and the same rule, and that test must be re-pinned, or it fails. The rubric stays the authority; the doc is a mirror, not a second wording.
4. **Surface it where agents read** — `AGENTS.md` gains ONE bullet in the existing "Where to read (one-line pointers into `docs/`)" list, in that section's pointer style: the rule named in a clause, pointing at `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (already the AGENTS.md pointer target for gate protocols) and at `rebar explain project.portability`. `explain` prints the rubric body including the matrix — verified in-session: `rebar explain project.portability | grep -n 'Platform and venue'` returns the matrix line, so the new cell and rule reach that surface. No restatement of the rubric text; AGENTS.md's keep-it-lean rule forbids it.

**Deliberately out of scope, with reasons.**
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is generated by `regenerate_criteria_guide`, which calls `load_criteria(repo_root="")` — the built-in registry, overlays excluded — and builds sections from registry `scenario`/`checklist`, not from `.rebar/prompts/*.md`. `project.portability` is an overlay with no section there, so regenerating produces NO diff. Not a deliverable; the generator runs only as a no-diff check.
- `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` is pinned by `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` at exactly 8 cases (`PORT-F1..F4`, `PORT-N1..N4`) with `coverage_threshold: 1.0`; a ninth CI case changes the corpus contract and needs its own live `rebar criteria eval` attestation run.
- `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md` covers the external LLM suite's provider matrix, not CI systems.

## Scope
- `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` — matrix cell + the no-CI-provider rule (the authoritative wording).
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` — pin the new matrix value and the new rule.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the hand-authored matrix mirror + the rule.
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py` — re-pin the mirrored matrix value and the rule.
- `AGENTS.md` — one pointer bullet.

## Testing
String-pinning alone would only prove the wording shipped, not that the reviewer acts on it, so detection efficacy is verified live as well.
- **Happy path:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` passes with the new `Platform and venue` value, and the new assertion finds the no-CI-provider rule in the rubric body.
- **Failure path:** the new assertion targets the rule's load-bearing phrase, so deleting the rule fails the test — verified by removing the phrase locally and watching it fail before restoring it.
- **Live detection check (the efficacy test):** create a scratch ticket whose plan schedules recurring work behind a GitHub-Actions-only trigger with no fallback, run `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 rebar review-plan <scratch>`, and confirm a `project.portability` finding naming the no-CI-provider shape is emitted; re-run against the pre-change rubric to confirm it did NOT fire before. That A/B distinguishes a working rule from present text. Both verdicts are recorded as a comment here and the scratch ticket closed.
- **Mirror parity:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py` passes against the updated `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, so the doc mirror cannot drift from the rubric.
- **Unchanged contracts:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py` must pass untouched, proving the eval corpus contract and the `project-portability` coaching move are not disturbed.
- **Generator no-diff:** re-running the criteria-guide generator leaves the tree clean, confirming the overlay-exclusion reasoning above rather than assuming it.
- **Gates:** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the `check_*` gates (notably `check_criteria_vocabulary.py`, which lints criterion wording), and the CI unit selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The rubric names both "CI under any provider" and "projects with NO CI provider at all" in its `Platform and venue` cell, and carries a rule stating that a capability whose only trigger is a specific CI system is not portable and needs an operation-linked or in-process fallback.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` pins both the new matrix value and the new rule, and passes.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md`'s mirrored matrix cell and rule match the rubric, and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py` is re-pinned and passes.
- [ ] A live `rebar review-plan` A/B on a scratch GitHub-Actions-only plan draws a `project.portability` finding with the new rubric and none with the old, with both verdicts recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` carries exactly one new bullet for the rule, in the existing one-line-pointer style, cross-linking `rebar explain project.portability` and restating no rubric text.
- [ ] Re-running the criteria-guide generator leaves the tree clean (the overlay criterion has no section there, so this change is correctly absent from it).
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py` pass unchanged; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the CI unit selection are green.
